exclude.description: Exclude paths (comma/space-separated or array). Same syntax as path: directory prefix ('test/'), filename with extension ('config.json'), or glob ('*.min.js', '**/*.{rs,go}'). A leading '!' is optional and ignored — both 'test/' and '!test/' work. Example: 'test/,*.min.js,!vendor/'.

caseSensitive.description: Force case-sensitive matching. Default uses smart-case (case-insensitive when pattern is all lowercase).

toolsAdded.name: fffind
toolsAdded.description: Fuzzy path search and glob search. Matches against the whole repo-relative path, not just the filename. Frecency-ranked, git-aware. Multi-word = narrower (AND). Default limit 30.

pattern.description: Fuzzy filename search and glob search. Frecency-ranked, git-aware. Multi-word = narrower (AND) not bound to order, use for multi word related concept search. Prefer this over ls/find/bash as the first exploration step whenever the user names a concept, feature, or symbol — it surfaces the relevant files in one call. Only use ls/read on a directory when you specifically need the alphabetical layout of an unknown repo, or when a concept search returned nothing.

path.description: Path constraint. Directory prefix (src/ or src/foo/), bare filename with extension (main.rs), or glob (*.ts, src/**/*.cc, {src,lib}/**). Applied to the full repo-relative path. Absolute, ~/, and ../ paths outside the workspace are also supported and searched with a separate index.

exclude.description: Exclude paths (comma/space-separated or array). Same syntax as path: directory prefix ('test/'), filename with extension ('config.json'), or glob ('*.min.js', '**/*.{rs,go}'). A leading '!' is optional and ignored — both 'test/' and '!test/' work. Example: 'test/,*.min.js,!vendor/'.

toolsAdded.name: advisor
toolsAdded.description: Escalate to a stronger reviewer model for guidance. When you need stronger judgment — a complex decision, an ambiguous failure, a problem you're circling without progress — escalate to the advisor model for guidance, then resume. Takes NO parameters — when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. The advisor sees the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

toolsAdded.name: compress
toolsAdded.description: Replace consumed conversation ranges with self-contained summaries you write, identified by their refs. content = ONE plain string holding ALL ranges — each block starts with its 'm00150–m00220 optional topic' header line followed by that block's summary (a valid JSON string — internal quotes \", newlines \n; a JSON-encoded array as that string is also accepted for gateways that stringify arrays). Batch multiple ranges into ONE call — do not split into one call per range. Use when content is genuinely consumed. Calling convention: if this environment only allows `run_code` to be called directly (code-mode/PTC harness), call this tool from inside a run_code program via the harness's generated SDK; otherwise call it directly as a tool. Context management is provided by billion-context — report billion-context problems at github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues.

content.description: ONE plain string holding ALL ranges to compress — each block starts with its 'm00150–m00220 optional topic' header line followed by that block's summary markdown (a valid JSON string: internal quotes \" and newlines \n; a JSON-encoded array as that string is also accepted). Batch multiple ranges into ONE call — do not split into one call per range.

toolsAdded.name: decompress
toolsAdded.description: Restores previously compressed content. Use when you need exact details lost in compression. By default restores one tier up. Use full:true for all the way to original messages. Use toFile to write to file instead of inflating context. Pass imageRef (an mNNNNN ref) to restore a stripped/folded image's original pixels to a file you open with the read tool; imageRef:"list" shows what is restorable. Calling convention: if this environment only allows `run_code` to be called directly (code-mode/PTC harness), call this tool from inside a run_code program via the harness's generated SDK; otherwise call it directly as a tool.

toFile.description: Optional: write content to file instead of context

full.description: Restore all the way to original messages

imageRef.description: Optional mNNNNN message ref whose IMAGE payload you want restored (an image that was stripped or folded away). Pass "list" to enumerate every image currently restorable. Restored images are written to host-readable files and their paths returned — open them with the read tool. Independent of blockId/range and of CCR.

toolsAdded.name: search_context
toolsAdded.description: Search through compressed block summaries by keyword. Use BEFORE decompressing to find the right block. Calling convention: if this environment only allows `run_code` to be called directly (code-mode/PTC harness), call this tool from inside a run_code program via the harness's generated SDK; otherwise call it directly as a tool.

toolsAdded.name: acp_status
toolsAdded.description: Show context usage and compressible ranges. No args = overview; pass scope/view/tool/sort/limit/archiveDetail for targeted listings. Calling convention: if this environment only allows `run_code` to be called directly (code-mode/PTC harness), call this tool from inside a run_code program via the harness's generated SDK; otherwise call it directly as a tool.

scope.description: "uncompressed": history outside active blocks; "compressed": block ledger; omit = default overview

view.description: "messages" for a per-message listing; "ranges" is the default

tool.description: With view:"messages": only list results of this tool name

archiveDetail.description: List pre-compaction archived blocks per-id instead of grouped by reason

toolsAdded.name: acp_cache
toolsAdded.description: Prompt-cache reconciliation: grand ledger (total input/cached/output, overall hit rate) with every request's miss split into new content / compression re-pay / upstream-ttl-or-client-rewrite (unattributed stable-prefix misses), plus per-fold economics (breakeven turns vs measured cadence). Defaults to a compact summary (totals + verdicts + anomalies only); pass detail="full" for every fold and its line-item breakdown. Read-only. Call when asked about cache hits, cache invalidation, or what compression costs. Calling convention: if this environment only allows `run_code` to be called directly (code-mode/PTC harness), call this tool from inside a run_code program via the harness's generated SDK; otherwise call it directly as a tool.

detail.description: "summary" (default): totals, verdicts, notable folds, anomalous requests only. "full": every retained fold and its line-item breakdown (most-recent window — the output states the cap).

toolsAdded.name: acp_read_original_image
toolsAdded.description: Read the ORIGINAL full-resolution image of a message whose picture was downscaled before reaching you. Beside each shrunken image there is a [bili] note quoting its mNNNNN ref and both sizes — pass that ref here. The original bytes are returned as an image attached to this result. The original can be much larger than the downscaled copy, so call this only when you actually need full-resolution detail (small text, colors, pixel alignment); the downscaled version is enough for most work.

ref.description: The mNNNNN message ref quoted in the [bili] downsample note beside the shrunken image.

toolsAdded.name: codegraph_explore
toolsAdded.description: PRIMARY TOOL — call FIRST for almost any question OR before an edit: how does X work, architecture, a bug, where/what is X, surveying an area, or the symbols you are about to change. Returns the verbatim source of the relevant symbols grouped by file in ONE capped call (Read-equivalent — treat the shown source as already Read; do NOT re-open those files), plus the call path among them. Query can be a natural-language question OR a bag of symbol/file names. Usually the ONLY call you need — more accurate context, in far fewer tokens and round-trips than a search/Read/Grep loop.

query.description: Symbol names, file names, or short code terms to explore (e.g., "AuthService loginUser session-manager", "GraphTraverser BFS impact traversal.ts"). For a flow question, name the symbols spanning the flow (e.g. "mutateElement renderScene"). A natural-language question works too — no prior codegraph_search needed.

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to include source code from (default: 12)

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project to query (or any directory inside it) — codegraph uses the nearest .codegraph/ index at or above that path. Omit to use this session's default project. Pass it to query a second codebase, or when the server root has no index of its own (e.g. a monorepo where only sub-projects are indexed, so there is no default project).

toolsAdded.name: ctx_execute
toolsAdded.description:
Example: `ctx_execute({language:"shell",code:"git log --oneline -5"})`. Required: language, code.
Write code that prints only the answer, not the raw data. Runs code in a sandboxed subprocess in the project directory (shell, powershell, javascript, typescript, python, or another runtime on PATH); only what the code prints comes back. For a large file, set `file` to its local path: the code gets it in the CTX_FILE environment variable. Set `intent` when output may be large: the matching sections come back and the full output is indexed for ctx_search. `timeoutMs` defaults to and caps at 600000; then the whole process tree is killed.

toolsAdded.name: ctx_batch
toolsAdded.description:
Example: `ctx_batch({commands:["git log --oneline -5"],queries:["recent changes"]})`. Required: commands, queries.
Runs several shell commands, then answers several search queries over their combined output, in one call. Use it to collect facts from more than one command at once, for example test results plus recent commits, when you need specific answers rather than the full text. Returns the matching sections and a one-line footer.

toolsAdded.name: ctx_index
toolsAdded.description:
Example: `ctx_index({path:"docs/api.md"})`. Required: one of path, content, url.
Stores content so it can be searched later: a local file or folder (nested .gitignore files are respected), raw text, or a URL, which is fetched and converted to Markdown. Use it for documentation or large files you will query more than once, then use ctx_search instead of reading the content again. Returns the source label and how many chunks were stored.

toolsAdded.name: ctx_search
toolsAdded.description:
Example: `ctx_search({queries:["auth middleware"]})`. Required: queries.
Searches content stored with ctx_index and earlier sandbox output in this project. Memory files such as AGENTS.md are searched too. Pass several queries in one call. By default it searches the current worktree; set `scope` to `project` for all worktrees or `session` for this session only. Results from the current session rank first, then by relevance, ranked with measurably better recall than plain keyword search. Set `sort` to `timeline` for oldest-first order across this session, prior sessions and memory, paged with `after`; `offset` is for relevance order only. Set `source` to `decision` to search only rows where the user answered a question. Every hit names its source. When nothing matches, the reply states the scope and how many sources are indexed.

toolsAdded.name: ctx_resume
toolsAdded.description:
Example: `ctx_resume({})`. Required: none.
Returns a summary of up to 2 KB for this session: the last task and user request, files changed, open errors, and search terms for ctx_search. A large row is shown as a pointer line instead of its full text; call `ctx_resume(seq: N)` with that line's number to read the full row. Call it with no `seq` to get the state block on demand. Use it after the conversation was compacted or resumed, before you repeat earlier work.

toolsAdded.name: ctx_stats
toolsAdded.description:
Example: `ctx_stats({})`. Required: none.
Reports the bytes context-mode kept out of the chat: a text report (bars, per tool, per agent) and a Markdown table. Show the text block to the user unchanged, in a code block. Use it when the user asks what it saved.

toolsAdded.name: ctx_doctor
toolsAdded.description:
Example: `ctx_doctor({})`. Required: none.
Checks this context-mode install and reports a table with one row per check: version, Node and node:sqlite, host config and hooks for this agent, MCP connection, project and worktree, database health, index contents, and hook timing. Each failed row names its cause, the fix and a docs link. Use it when the user asks whether context-mode works, or after a context-mode error. Run each Fix first, then call ctx_doctor again. If a FAIL stays, show the user the report file it names (it holds paths and environment details) and ask before you run the printed gh issue command.

toolsAdded.name: ctx_upgrade
toolsAdded.description:
Example: `ctx_upgrade({})`. Required: none.
Updates context-mode to the latest release for this agent and rewrites only context-mode's own entries in the host config. User entries and user settings such as hook timeouts are kept, and old entries are erased. Returns a table of what changed and whether a restart is needed. Use it only when the user asks to update context-mode.

toolsAdded.name: ctx_purge
toolsAdded.description:
Example: `ctx_purge({source:"old-docs"})`. Required: one of session, source, project.
Deletes stored data: one session, one indexed source, or everything stored for this project. This cannot be undone. Use it only when the user asks to forget or reset data.

content.text: Add robust C# support to OXIDE using the existing language architecture. Cover declarations, namespaces, imports, inheritance, references, and conservative cross-file resolution, with working CLI navigation and context retrieval. Research the grammar and C# semantics first, validate against real .NET repositories and compiler-backed oracles where practical, preserve existing language behavior, and benchmark indexing and retrieval before acceptance.

"""Java language slice: tree-sitter syntax facts (docs/java.md); resolution is in
``java_resolve``, the facts' cache codec in ``java_facts``.

Symbols are the member types of a file and their methods, constructors and annotation
elements, nested as declared. Local and anonymous classes are not symbols: each is a
type scope without a declaration (and an enum constant's body is one too), whose
members resolution treats as unknown. A variable bound anywhere in a scope keeps its
declared type when every binding of the name agrees (``var``, primitives and arrays have
none); one compiled query collects every fact in C, and Python assigns each captured
node to its innermost scope.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import tree_sitter_java
from tree_sitter import Language, Node, Parser, Query, QueryCursor

from oxide.core.languages.nesting import Nesting
from oxide.core.languages.python import TOO_DEEP, Use, syntax_diagnostics, too_deep

VERSION = "oxide-java-v2"
# The JSON shape of ``Parsed`` that generations retain for reuse; bump on any change.
FACTS_VERSION = "oxide-java-facts-v1"
_TYPE_KINDS = {
    "class_declaration": "class",
    "interface_declaration": "interface",
    "enum_declaration": "enum",
    "record_declaration": "record",
    "annotation_type_declaration": "annotation",
}
TYPE_KINDS = frozenset(_TYPE_KINDS.values())
_HEADER = ("type_parameters", "superclass", "super_interfaces", "extends_interfaces", "permits")
KINDS = frozenset({*TYPE_KINDS, "method", "constructor"})
# JUnit 4/5 and TestNG test annotations, by simple name.
TEST_ANNOTATIONS = frozenset(
    {"Test", "ParameterizedTest", "RepeatedTest", "TestFactory"} | {"TestTemplate"}
)
_COMMENTS = ("line_comment", "block_comment")

LANGUAGE = Language(tree_sitter_java.language())
_QUERY = Query(
    LANGUAGE,
    f"""
    (package_declaration [(identifier) (scoped_identifier)] @package)
    (import_declaration) @import
    [{" ".join(f"({t})" for t in _TYPE_KINDS)}] @type
    [(method_declaration) (constructor_declaration) (compact_constructor_declaration)
      (annotation_type_element_declaration)] @member
    (object_creation_expression (class_body)) @anonymous
    (enum_constant body: (class_body) @constant_body)
    (enum_constant name: (identifier) @constant)
    (method_invocation) @call
    (object_creation_expression) @new
    [(type_identifier) (scoped_type_identifier)] @ref
    (marker_annotation name: _ @ref)
    (annotation name: _ @ref)
    (type_parameter (type_identifier) @type_parameter)
    [(formal_parameter) (catch_formal_parameter) (enhanced_for_statement) (resource)
      (instanceof_expression name: _) (type_pattern) (record_pattern_component)] @var
    (spread_parameter (variable_declarator name: (identifier) @untyped))
    (inferred_parameters (identifier) @untyped)
    (lambda_expression parameters: (identifier) @untyped)
    [(local_variable_declaration) (field_declaration) (constant_declaration)] @vars
    """,
)
_BROKEN = Query(LANGUAGE, "(ERROR) @error (MISSING) @missing")

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)

"""Java syntax facts' cache codec; extraction is in ``java``."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any

from oxide.core.languages.java import (
    KINDS,
    TYPE_KINDS,
    Call,
    Decl,
    Import,
    Parsed,
    Scope,
)
from oxide.core.languages.python import Use, as_list


def encode(parsed: Parsed) -> list[Any]:
    scopes = [
        [
            s.parent,
            s.decl and [getattr(s.decl, f) for f in Decl.__slots__],
            [[u.name, u.start, u.end] for u in s.supers],
            [[name, kind] for name, kind in sorted(s.bound.items())],
            sorted(s.types),
            [[c.name, c.start, c.end, c.arity] for c in s.calls],
            [[u.name, u.start, u.end] for u in s.refs],
        ]
        for s in parsed.scopes
    ]
    imports = [[i.static, i.path, i.wildcard, i.start, i.end] for i in parsed.imports]
    return [parsed.package, imports, scopes, parsed.diagnostics]


def decode(value: Any, size: int) -> Parsed:
    """The inverse of ``encode`` for a file of ``size`` bytes. Cached facts come from
    disk: anything ``parse`` could not have produced raises ValueError, and the caller
    parses instead."""
    try:
        package, imports, scopes, diagnostics = as_list(value)
        parsed = Parsed(
            package,
            [Import(*as_list(i)) for i in as_list(imports)],
            [
                Scope(
                    parent,
                    None if decl is None else Decl(*as_list(decl)),
                    [Use(*as_list(u)) for u in as_list(supers)],
                    {name: kind for name, kind in map(as_list, as_list(bound))},
                    set(as_list(types)),
                    [Call(*as_list(c)) for c in as_list(calls)],
                    [Use(*as_list(u)) for u in as_list(refs)],
                )
                for parent, decl, supers, bound, types, calls, refs in map(as_list, as_list(scopes))
            ],
            as_list(diagnostics),
        )
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as error:
        raise ValueError(f"malformed parse facts: {error}") from None
    if not _sound(parsed, size):
        raise ValueError("parse facts are ill-typed, out of bounds or not a scope tree")
    return parsed

_DOTTED = re.compile(rf"{_NAME}(?:\.{_NAME})*")

"""Conservative Java resolution over every ``.java`` file of one capture (docs/java.md).

A package is the files sharing a package declaration, keyed ``module:java:<package>``;
default-package files form one package per directory and no module. Names resolve the
way javac scopes them, over captured source only: enclosing classes and their captured
supertypes, the file's types and single-type imports, the package, then on-demand
imports. A member lookup that reaches a supertype outside the capture, or a local or
anonymous class, is unknown and stays unresolved rather than guessed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import bisect
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from oxide.core.languages.java import TYPE_KINDS, Call, Parsed, Scope
from oxide.core.languages.python import Use
from oxide.core.languages.python_resolve import Edge, Res, edge_target, structural
from oxide.models import Entity, RelationKind, SourceRef

# Methods a type has without declaring them, by kind.
_OBJECT = frozenset(
    {"clone", "equals", "finalize", "getClass", "hashCode", "notify", "notifyAll", "toString"}
    | {"wait"}
)
_ENUM = {"compareTo", "describeConstable", "getDeclaringClass", "name", "ordinal", "valueOf"}
_IMPLICIT = {"enum": _OBJECT | _ENUM | {"values"}, "annotation": _OBJECT | {"annotationType"}}
_METHOD = frozenset({"method"})
_IMPORTABLE = frozenset(TYPE_KINDS | _METHOD)

type Site = tuple[int, int]  # (file, scope)
type Package = tuple[str, str]  # ("", package), or (directory, "") for the default package
type Found = list[Site] | None  # None: unknown, so unresolved; []: certainly none
type Variable = tuple[Site, str | None]  # the declaring scope and the declared type


def module_key(package: str) -> str:
    return f"module:java:{package}"


def symbol_keys(path: str, parsed: Parsed) -> list[str | None]:
    """Per scope, ``symbol:<path>#Outer.Inner.m``: the file key for scope 0, None for a
    local or anonymous class. Equal segments (overloads) take ``~n`` in source order,
    and members nest under their owner's segment, ordinal included."""
    keys: list[str | None] = [f"file:{path}"]
    segments = [""]
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    for s in parsed.scopes[1:]:
        if s.decl is None or s.parent is None:
            keys.append(None)
            segments.append("")
            continue
        owner = segments[s.parent]
        segment = f"{owner}.{s.decl.name}" if owner else s.decl.name
        n = seen.get(segment, 0)
        seen[segment] = n + 1
        segment += f"~{n}" if n else ""
        segments.append(segment)
        keys.append(f"symbol:{path}#{segment}")
    return keys


@dataclass(slots=True)
class _File:
    path: str
    digest: str
    parsed: Parsed
    keys: list[str | None]
    owners: list[str]  # per scope, the key of the nearest declared scope (or the file)
    package: Package
    single: dict[str, list[Site]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # [] when not captured
    demand: list[Site | str] = field(default_factory=list)  # a type, or a package
    statics: dict[str, list[Site]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # static member -> owners
    static_demand: list[Site] = field(default_factory=list)

def _sound(parsed: Parsed, size: int) -> bool:
    """What ``parse`` guarantees: in-bounds spans, typed values, a scope tree whose
    parents precede their children, identifier and dotted names, so identities stay
    unique and lookups well-formed."""

    def span(a: Any, b: Any) -> bool:
        return type(a) is int and type(b) is int and 0 <= a <= b <= size

    def dotted(v: Any) -> bool:
        return type(v) is str and _DOTTED.fullmatch(v) is not None

    def texts(*values: Any) -> bool:
        return all(type(v) is str for v in values)

    scopes = parsed.scopes
    if not scopes or scopes[0].parent is not None or scopes[0].decl is not None:
        return False
    for k, s in enumerate(scopes):
        d = s.decl
        if k and not (type(s.parent) is int and 0 <= s.parent < k):
            return False
        owner = scopes[s.parent].decl if k and type(s.parent) is int else None
        if d is not None and not (
            k
            and type(d.kind) is str
            and d.kind in KINDS
            # members belong to a declared type; types to one or to the file
            and (owner.kind in TYPE_KINDS if owner else s.parent == 0 and d.kind in TYPE_KINDS)
            and dotted(d.name)
            and "." not in d.name
            and span(d.start, d.end)
            and texts(d.signature)
            and type(d.arity) is int
            and d.arity >= 0
            and {type(d.varargs), type(d.test)} == {bool}
        ):
            return False
        calls = all(
            span(c.start, c.end) and texts(c.name) and type(c.arity) is int for c in s.calls
        )
        if not (
            calls
            and all(span(u.start, u.end) and dotted(u.name) for u in (*s.supers, *s.refs))
            and all(dotted(n) and (t is None or dotted(t)) for n, t in s.bound.items())
            and texts(*s.types)
        ):
            return False
    return (
        (parsed.package == "" or dotted(parsed.package))
        and texts(*parsed.diagnostics)
        and all(
            type(i.static) is bool
            and dotted(i.path)
            and type(i.wildcard) is bool
            and span(i.start, i.end)
            for i in parsed.imports
        )
    )

def dialect(path: str) -> Dialect | None:
    """The language slice and grammar that parse ``path``, None when none does."""
    if path.endswith(".go"):
        return "go"
    if path.endswith(".rs"):
        return "rust"
    if path.endswith(".java"):

    if path.endswith((".c", ".h")):

    if path.endswith(CPP_SUFFIXES):

Symbols are the member types of a file and their methods, constructors and annotation

type scope without a declaration (and an enum constant's body is one too), whose
members resolution treats as unknown. A variable bound anywhere in a scope keeps its

"""Conservative Java resolution over every ``.java`` file of one capture (docs/java.md).

A package is the files sharing a package declaration, keyed ``module:java:<package>``;
default-package files form one package per directory and no module. Names resolve the
way javac scopes them, over captured source only: enclosing classes and their captured
supertypes, the file's types and single-type imports, the package, then on-demand
imports. A member lookup that reaches a supertype outside the capture, or a local or
anonymous class, is unknown and stays unresolved rather than guessed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import bisect
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from oxide.core.languages.java import TYPE_KINDS, Call, Parsed, Scope
from oxide.core.languages.python import Use
from oxide.core.languages.python_resolve import Edge, Res, edge_target, structural
from oxide.models import Entity, RelationKind, SourceRef

# Methods a type has without declaring them, by kind.
_OBJECT = frozenset(
    {"clone", "equals", "finalize", "getClass", "hashCode", "notify", "notifyAll", "toString"}
    | {"wait"}
)
_ENUM = {"compareTo", "describeConstable", "getDeclaringClass", "name", "ordinal", "valueOf"}
_IMPLICIT = {"enum": _OBJECT | _ENUM | {"values"}, "annotation": _OBJECT | {"annotationType"}}
_METHOD = frozenset({"method"})
_IMPORTABLE = frozenset(TYPE_KINDS | _METHOD)

type Site = tuple[int, int]  # (file, scope)
type Package = tuple[str, str]  # ("", package), or (directory, "") for the default package
type Found = list[Site] | None  # None: unknown, so unresolved; []: certainly none
type Variable = tuple[Site, str | None]  # the declaring scope and the declared type


def module_key(package: str) -> str:
    return f"module:java:{package}"


def symbol_keys(path: str, parsed: Parsed) -> list[str | None]:
    """Per scope, ``symbol:<path>#Outer.Inner.m``: the file key for scope 0, None for a
    local or anonymous class. Equal segments (overloads) take ``~n`` in source order,
    and members nest under their owner's segment, ordinal included."""
    keys: list[str | None] = [f"file:{path}"]
    segments = [""]
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    for s in parsed.scopes[1:]:
        if s.decl is None or s.parent is None:
            keys.append(None)
            segments.append("")
            continue
        owner = segments[s.parent]
        segment = f"{owner}.{s.decl.name}" if owner else s.decl.name
        n = seen.get(segment, 0)
        seen[segment] = n + 1
        segment += f"~{n}" if n else ""
        segments.append(segment)
        keys.append(f"symbol:{path}#{segment}")
    return keys

"""Java syntax facts' cache codec; extraction is in ``java``."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any

from oxide.core.languages.java import (
    KINDS,
    TYPE_KINDS,
    Call,
    Decl,
    Import,
    Parsed,
    Scope,
)
from oxide.core.languages.python import Use, as_list


def encode(parsed: Parsed) -> list[Any]:
    scopes = [
        [
            s.parent,
            s.decl and [getattr(s.decl, f) for f in Decl.__slots__],
            [[u.name, u.start, u.end] for u in s.supers],
            [[name, kind] for name, kind in sorted(s.bound.items())],
            sorted(s.types),
            [[c.name, c.start, c.end, c.arity] for c in s.calls],
            [[u.name, u.start, u.end] for u in s.refs],
        ]
        for s in parsed.scopes
    ]
    imports = [[i.static, i.path, i.wildcard, i.start, i.end] for i in parsed.imports]
    return [parsed.package, imports, scopes, parsed.diagnostics]


def decode(value: Any, size: int) -> Parsed:
    """The inverse of ``encode`` for a file of ``size`` bytes. Cached facts come from
    disk: anything ``parse`` could not have produced raises ValueError, and the caller
    parses instead."""
    try:
        package, imports, scopes, diagnostics = as_list(value)
        parsed = Parsed(
            package,
            [Import(*as_list(i)) for i in as_list(imports)],
            [
                Scope(
                    parent,
                    None if decl is None else Decl(*as_list(decl)),
                    [Use(*as_list(u)) for u in as_list(supers)],
                    {name: kind for name, kind in map(as_list, as_list(bound))},
                    set(as_list(types)),
                    [Call(*as_list(c)) for c in as_list(calls)],
                    [Use(*as_list(u)) for u in as_list(refs)],
                )
                for parent, decl, supers, bound, types, calls, refs in map(as_list, as_list(scopes))
            ],
            as_list(diagnostics),
        )
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as error:
        raise ValueError(f"malformed parse facts: {error}") from None
    if not _sound(parsed, size):
        raise ValueError("parse facts are ill-typed, out of bounds or not a scope tree")
    return parsed

return parsed


_NAME = r"(?!\d)[\w$]+"
_DOTTED = re.compile(rf"{_NAME}(?:\.{_NAME})*")


def _sound(parsed: Parsed, size: int) -> bool:
    """What ``parse`` guarantees: in-bounds spans, typed values, a scope tree whose
    parents precede their children, identifier and dotted names, so identities stay
    unique and lookups well-formed."""

    def span(a: Any, b: Any) -> bool:
        return type(a) is int and type(b) is int and 0 <= a <= b <= size

    def dotted(v: Any) -> bool:
        return type(v) is str and _DOTTED.fullmatch(v) is not None

    def texts(*values: Any) -> bool:
        return all(type(v) is str for v in values)

    scopes = parsed.scopes
    if not scopes or scopes[0].parent is not None or scopes[0].decl is not None:
        return False
    for k, s in enumerate(scopes):
        d = s.decl
        if k and not (type(s.parent) is int and 0 <= s.parent < k):
            return False
        owner = scopes[s.parent].decl if k and type(s.parent) is int else None
        if d is not None and not (
            k
            and type(d.kind) is str
            and d.kind in KINDS
            # members belong to a declared type; types to one or to the file
            and (owner.kind in TYPE_KINDS if owner else s.parent == 0 and d.kind in TYPE_KINDS)
            and dotted(d.name)
            and "." not in d.name
            and span(d.start, d.end)
            and texts(d.signature)
            and type(d.arity) is int
            and d.arity >= 0
            and {type(d.varargs), type(d.test)} == {bool}
        ):
            return False
        calls = all(
            span(c.start, c.end) and texts(c.name) and type(c.arity) is int for c in s.calls
        )
        if not (
            calls
            and all(span(u.start, u.end) and dotted(u.name) for u in (*s.supers, *s.refs))
            and all(dotted(n) and (t is None or dotted(t)) for n, t in s.bound.items())
            and texts(*s.types)
        ):
            return False
    return (
        (parsed.package == "" or dotted(parsed.package))
        and texts(*parsed.diagnostics)
        and all(
            type(i.static) is bool
            and dotted(i.path)
            and type(i.wildcard) is bool
            and span(i.start, i.end)
            for i in parsed.imports
        )
    )

"""Innermost-scope lookup by byte offset, shared by the language slices."""

from __future__ import annotations

import bisect


class Nesting:
    """The innermost scope whose body holds a byte, in O(log depth).

    Scope 0 is the whole file. Bodies nest, so the innermost scope holding a byte is an
    ancestor-or-self of the last body starting at or before it, and ancestors' bodies
    end no earlier. ``jumps[k][j]`` is the 2**j-th ancestor of ``k``: skipping the
    ancestors that end at or before the byte takes O(log depth), where one parent at
    a time is quadratic after a deep nest.
    """

    def __init__(self, size: int) -> None:
        self.bodies: list[tuple[int, int]] = []  # (body start, scope), sorted
        self.ends = [size]
        self.parents = [0]
        self.jumps: list[list[int]] = [[]]

    def add(self, parent: int, body: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
        own = len(self.ends)
        up = [parent]
        while len(self.jumps[up[-1]]) >= len(up):
            up.append(self.jumps[up[-1]][len(up) - 1])
        self.ends.append(body[1])
        self.parents.append(parent)
        self.jumps.append(up)
        bisect.insort(self.bodies, (body[0], own))

    def scope_at(self, at: int) -> int:
        i = bisect.bisect_right(self.bodies, (at, len(self.ends))) - 1
        k = self.bodies[i][1] if i >= 0 else 0
        if not k or at < self.ends[k]:
            return k
        for j in range(len(self.jumps[k]) - 1, -1, -1):
            if j < len(self.jumps[k]) and (up := self.jumps[k][j]) and self.ends[up] <= at:
                k = up
        return self.parents[k]

"""C# syntax facts' cache codec; extraction is in ``csharp``."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any

from oxide.core.languages.csharp import (
    KINDS,
    TYPE_KINDS,
    Call,
    Decl,
    Import,
    Parsed,
    Scope,
)
from oxide.core.languages.python import Use, as_list


def encode(parsed: Parsed) -> list[Any]:
    scopes = [
        [
            s.parent,
            s.decl and [getattr(s.decl, f) for f in Decl.__slots__],
            [[u.name, u.start, u.end] for u in s.supers],
            [[name, kind] for name, kind in sorted(s.bound.items())],
            sorted(s.types),
            [[c.name, c.start, c.end, c.arity] for c in s.calls],
            [[u.name, u.start, u.end] for u in s.refs],
            [[u.name, u.start, u.end] for u in s.attrs],
        ]
        for s in parsed.scopes
    ]
    imports = [[getattr(i, f) for f in Import.__slots__] for i in parsed.imports]
    return [imports, scopes, parsed.diagnostics]


def decode(value: Any, size: int) -> Parsed:
    """The inverse of ``encode`` for a file of ``size`` bytes. Cached facts come from
    disk: anything ``parse`` could not have produced raises ValueError, and the caller
    parses instead."""
    try:
        imports, scopes, diagnostics = as_list(value)
        parsed = Parsed(
            [Import(*as_list(i)) for i in as_list(imports)],
            [
                Scope(
                    parent,
                    None if decl is None else Decl(*as_list(decl)),
                    [Use(*as_list(u)) for u in as_list(supers)],
                    {name: kind for name, kind in map(as_list, as_list(bound))},
                    set(as_list(types)),
                    [Call(*as_list(c)) for c in as_list(calls)],
                    [Use(*as_list(u)) for u in as_list(refs)],
                    [Use(*as_list(u)) for u in as_list(attrs)],
                )
                for parent, decl, supers, bound, types, calls, refs, attrs in map(
                    as_list, as_list(scopes)
                )
            ],
            as_list(diagnostics),
        )
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as error:
        raise ValueError(f"malformed parse facts: {error}") from None
    if not _sound(parsed, size):
        raise ValueError("parse facts are ill-typed, out of bounds or not a scope tree")
    return parsed


_NAME = r"(?!\d)\w+"
_DOTTED = re.compile(rf"{_NAME}(?:\.{_NAME})*")
_NAMESPACE = re.compile(rf"(?:{_NAME}(?:\.{_NAME})*)?")


def _sound(parsed: Parsed, size: int) -> bool:
    """What ``parse`` guarantees: in-bounds spans, typed values, a scope tree whose
    parents precede their children, identifier and dotted names, so identities stay
    unique and lookups well-formed."""

    def span(a: Any, b: Any) -> bool:
        return type(a) is int and type(b) is int and 0 <= a <= b <= size

    def dotted(v: Any) -> bool:
        return type(v) is str and _DOTTED.fullmatch(v) is not None

    def namespace(v: Any) -> bool:
        return type(v) is str and _NAMESPACE.fullmatch(v) is not None

    def texts(*values: Any) -> bool:
        return all(type(v) is str for v in values)

    def count(v: Any) -> bool:
        return type(v) is int and v >= 0

    scopes = parsed.scopes
    if not scopes or scopes[0].parent is not None or scopes[0].decl is not None:
        return False
    for k, s in enumerate(scopes):
        d = s.decl
        if k and not (type(s.parent) is int and 0 <= s.parent < k):
            return False
        owner = scopes[s.parent].decl if k and type(s.parent) is int else None
        if d is not None and not (
            k
            and type(d.kind) is str
            and d.kind in KINDS
            # members belong to a declared type; types to one or to the file
            and (owner.kind in TYPE_KINDS if owner else s.parent == 0 and d.kind in TYPE_KINDS)
            and dotted(d.name)
            and "." not in d.name
            and span(d.start, d.end)
            and texts(d.signature)
            and namespace(d.ns)
            and count(d.tparams)
            and count(d.arity)
            and count(d.optional)
            and d.optional <= d.arity
            and {type(d.varargs), type(d.test)} == {bool}
        ):
            return False
        calls = all(
            span(c.start, c.end) and texts(c.name) and type(c.arity) is int for c in s.calls
        )
        if not (
            calls
            and all(
                span(u.start, u.end) and dotted(u.name) for u in (*s.supers, *s.refs, *s.attrs)
            )
            and all(dotted(n) and (t is None or dotted(t)) for n, t in s.bound.items())
            and texts(*s.types)
        ):
            return False
    return texts(*parsed.diagnostics) and all(
        i.kind in ("using", "static", "alias")
        and dotted(i.path)
        and type(i.alias) is str
        and (i.alias == "") == (i.kind != "alias")
        and namespace(i.ns)
        and type(i.is_global) is bool
        and span(i.start, i.end)
        for i in parsed.imports
    )

"""Conservative Java resolution over every ``.java`` file of one capture (docs/java.md).

A package is the files sharing a package declaration, keyed ``module:java:<package>``;
default-package files form one package per directory and no module. Names resolve the
way javac scopes them, over captured source only: enclosing classes and their captured
supertypes, the file's types and single-type imports, the package, then on-demand
imports. A member lookup that reaches a supertype outside the capture, or a local or
anonymous class, is unknown and stays unresolved rather than guessed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import bisect
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from oxide.core.languages.java import TYPE_KINDS, Call, Parsed, Scope
from oxide.core.languages.python import Use
from oxide.core.languages.python_resolve import Edge, Res, edge_target, structural
from oxide.models import Entity, RelationKind, SourceRef

# Methods a type has without declaring them, by kind.
_OBJECT = frozenset(
    {"clone", "equals", "finalize", "getClass", "hashCode", "notify", "notifyAll", "toString"}
    | {"wait"}
)
_ENUM = {"compareTo", "describeConstable", "getDeclaringClass", "name", "ordinal", "valueOf"}
_IMPLICIT = {"enum": _OBJECT | _ENUM | {"values"}, "annotation": _OBJECT | {"annotationType"}}
_METHOD = frozenset({"method"})
_IMPORTABLE = frozenset(TYPE_KINDS | _METHOD)

type Site = tuple[int, int]  # (file, scope)
type Package = tuple[str, str]  # ("", package), or (directory, "") for the default package
type Found = list[Site] | None  # None: unknown, so unresolved; []: certainly none
type Variable = tuple[Site, str | None]  # the declaring scope and the declared type


def module_key(package: str) -> str:
    return f"module:java:{package}"


def symbol_keys(path: str, parsed: Parsed) -> list[str | None]:
    """Per scope, ``symbol:<path>#Outer.Inner.m``: the file key for scope 0, None for a
    local or anonymous class. Equal segments (overloads) take ``~n`` in source order,
    and members nest under their owner's segment, ordinal included."""
    keys: list[str | None] = [f"file:{path}"]
    segments = [""]
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    for s in parsed.scopes[1:]:
        if s.decl is None or s.parent is None:
            keys.append(None)
            segments.append("")
            continue
        owner = segments[s.parent]
        segment = f"{owner}.{s.decl.name}" if owner else s.decl.name
        n = seen.get(segment, 0)
        seen[segment] = n + 1
        segment += f"~{n}" if n else ""
        segments.append(segment)
        keys.append(f"symbol:{path}#{segment}")
    return keys

# OXIDE development workflow

Commands and verification for OXIDE v2, loaded on demand from the root
`AGENTS.md` routing table. Older docs and code comments that cite
"`AGENTS.md`" for a command or harness detail mean this file.

## Default loop

Read the code, change it, add or adjust a test, run `mise run verify`. That is the
whole process for features, fixes, language work and refactors. Only changes that
claim a retrieval/routing/packing quality or performance improvement also need the
ContextBench or `scripts/bench.py` runs below (see `AGENTS.md`).

## Review tiers

Run `mise run tier` on the final diff. It prints `tier=N` and the applicable rubric filenames.
Tiers combine by maximum: unclassified paths default to tier 1; Markdown paths are tier 0 unless a tier-2 path rule matches.

| Tier | Scope | Required before commit |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Documentation changes, except agent/review/spec policy | `mise run verify` |
| 1 | Tests, ordinary source/configuration paths, and unknown paths | Tier 0 plus an independent zero-context diff review against the printed `docs/review/` rubrics |
| 2 | Public API, capture/storage/core policy, frozen evaluation fixtures, test harness, dependencies, CI/agent configuration, review classifier and architecture authorities | Tier 1 plus a short intent spec in `docs/superpowers/specs/`, reviewed by a zero-context agent before implementation for features/behavior changes. Bug fixes restoring documented behavior do not need a new spec. |

Cursor reviews pull requests. There is no Claude Code review check in CI.
`mise run tier` is local guidance before commit; it is not a GitHub gate.
CI runs `mise run verify` on every PR. `Verify` is the required status check. Agents retain autonomous implementation and commits; no per-change human approval is added.

## Commands

[Mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/installing-mise.html) is the one entrypoint;
`mise.toml` pins uv, and `.python-version` pins the development Python (uv
installs it). CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs exactly `mise run verify`;
`.github/workflows/platforms.yml` runs the suite and an installed-artifact smoke on
Linux, Windows and both macOS architectures ([docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)).

```bash
mise run bootstrap     # uv sync --locked + `oxide setup` (pinned FTS extension, sha256-checked)
                       #   + ContextBench corpora at pinned commits (git, cached)
mise run verify        # everything, in order, stopping at the first failure:
mise run lint          #   ruff check + ruff format --check
mise run typecheck     #   mypy --strict over src/ and tests/python/
mise run test          #   pytest (tests/python/)
```

`uv run pyrefly check` is an optional second type checker (`[tool.pyrefly]` in
`pyproject.toml`). It is not part of `verify` or CI; mypy `--strict` stays the gate.
On 2026-10-31 it reported 32 errors.

Use `uv run …` for anything else (`uv run oxide index <path>`, `uv run pytest -k name`).
`uv run oxide mcp --repo <path>` serves the single `oxide_search` tool over stdio (`--http` for
stateless HTTP on loopback); `docs/public-api.md` § MCP has the contract.
`uv run python scripts/bench.py <corpus>` is the reproducible latency and
peak-RSS benchmark: fresh processes and private data, cold and warm definitions
in its docstring, and a JSON report with the corpus identity and environment.
Run it under the limits below; recorded runs are in `docs/migration-audit/bench/` at commit `013e791`.
`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py run [--out DIR]` is the context-quality
harness (entry-point, routing and packing metrics at 256/1,024/4,096 units);
`tests/python/test_contextbench.py` gates it in `mise run verify` against the latest
frozen `fixtures/eval/contextbench-py/baseline-vN/` (`contextbench.BASELINE`); the protocol (splits, gate
Core wiring and tests pass. Now run the full verify to see what the other languages' tests expect (docs, smoke, baselines).

# Java source support

`oxide-java-v1` adds Java as a language slice of the existing engine:
`core/languages/java.py` extracts syntax facts with `tree-sitter-java==0.23.5`, and
`core/languages/java_resolve.py` resolves them over the whole capture. No JDK, `javac`,
build tool (Maven, Gradle), dependency download or repository code runs during
indexing or querying. The ordinary Python API, CLI, retrieval, graph, router and context
packer serve these files unchanged, and MCP remains exactly one tool, `oxide_search`,
with `search`, `context` and `impact` modes.

## Extraction and identity

`.java` files report `FileInfo.language == "java"`. Declared types and their members
become symbols, nested as written:

| Java declaration | Kind | Key segment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `class C` | `class` | `C` |
| `interface I` | `interface` | `I` |
| `enum E` | `enum` | `E` |
| `record R(...)` | `record` | `R` |
| `@interface A` | `annotation` | `A` |
| a method, abstract or interface method, or annotation element of `C` | `method` | `C.m` |
| a constructor of `C`, compact canonical constructors included | `constructor` | `C.C` |
| a member type `N` of `C` | its kind | `C.N` |

Keys are `symbol:<path>#<segment>`. A member's physical parent is its type, and a
top-level type's is the file. Overloads and other equal segments take `~n` in source
order (`Store.put`, `Store.put~1`), and members nest under the ordinal'd segment.
Entity names are the plain identifiers. Not symbols: fields, enum constants, initializer
blocks, local classes (declared in a method body) and anonymous classes. Their code
stays in the enclosing symbol, and calls inside them come from it.

A declaration's range is its tree-sitter node: modifiers and annotations included,
Javadoc excluded. Its signature is the header up to the body, without annotations, with
whitespace collapsed (`public class Store extends AbstractStore implements Backend`,
`public String get(Key key)`, `int seconds() default 60`).

A package is every `.java` file with the same package declaration, wherever its
directory: `module:java:<package>`, named by the package, so `src/main/java` and
`src/test/java` halves of one package are one module. Modules `contain_logical` their
files and `define` their top-level types. Default-package files form one package per
directory for resolution and have no module.

Test methods are methods annotated `@Test`, `@ParameterizedTest`, `@RepeatedTest`,
`@TestFactory` or `@TestTemplate`, matched by simple name, so the annotations of JUnit 4,
JUnit 5 and TestNG all count, qualified or not. A resolved call made inside a test,
including its lambdas and anonymous classes, adds `tested_by`, the same heuristic as the
other slices.

## Resolution

Everything below follows the Java Language Specification's scoping and javac's
compile-time lookup, applied to the captured source only. Nothing runs a type checker.
A lookup that would need one, or that reaches code outside the capture, is unresolved
rather than guessed.

- **Types.** A simple type name resolves in javac's order: type parameters and local
  classes, which are opaque; member types of the enclosing classes, innermost first,
  including types inherited from captured supertypes; then the file's own top-level

# C# source support

`oxide-csharp-v1` adds C# as a language slice of the existing engine:
`core/languages/csharp.py` extracts syntax facts with `tree-sitter-c-sharp==0.23.1`
(helpers in `csharp_syntax.py`, the facts' cache codec in `csharp_facts.py`), and
`core/languages/csharp_resolve.py` resolves them over the whole capture. No .NET SDK,
MSBuild, NuGet restore or repository code runs during indexing or querying. API, CLI,
retrieval, router and packer are unchanged; MCP stays the one `oxide_search` tool.

## Extraction and identity

`.cs` files report `FileInfo.language == "csharp"`. Types and their members become
symbols, nested as written:

| C# declaration | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `class`, `struct`, `interface`, `enum`, `record` (also `record struct`), `delegate` | the same word |
| method, constructor, destructor, operator and conversion operator | `method`, `constructor`, `destructor`, `operator` |
| property, indexer (named `this`), event, field, enum member | `property`, `indexer`, `event`, `field`, `enum_member` |

Keys are `symbol:<path>#Outer.Inner.member`; equal segments (overloads, operators) take
`~n` in source order. Operators are named as the runtime does (`op_Addition`,
`op_Implicit`). A multi-declarator field is one symbol per variable. Local functions,
lambdas and anonymous types are not symbols; their code stays in the enclosing symbol.
A declaration's range is its tree-sitter node (attributes included, comments excluded);
its signature is the header without attributes or body, whitespace collapsed.

Namespaces are not symbols. A namespace is every type declared in it, wherever the
file: `module:csharp:<namespace>`, which `contain_logical`s those files and `define`s
their top-level types. Block and file-scoped (`namespace A;`) forms, nesting and
`global::` are understood; the global namespace has no module. Partial types across
files merge into one hierarchy for resolution.

Test methods carry an xUnit, NUnit or MSTest attribute (`Fact`, `Theory`, `Test`,
`TestCase`, `TestMethod`, `DataTestMethod`, …) by simple name, with or without the
`Attribute` suffix; a resolved call inside one adds `tested_by`.

## Resolution

Following the C# name-lookup order over captured source only; anything that would need
a type checker or reaches outside the capture is left unresolved, not guessed.

- **Types** resolve through type parameters (opaque), nested and inherited member types,
  then each enclosing namespace outward: its own types, `using A = X;` aliases, and
  `using N;` namespaces (`global using` applies to every file), then the global
  namespace. An ambiguous name stays unresolved.
- **`using static T;`** brings static members of `T` into scope for unqualified calls.
- **Attributes** resolve as `N` or `NAttribute`.
- **Members** are looked up on the nearest declaring type of the captured hierarchy
  (base class, interfaces, partial parts); `this.m`, `base.m`, `new T(...)` (resolves
  to `T`), qualified `A.B.m`, locals/fields/properties with a declared type and
  `var`-free typed locals. Calls are filtered by arity, honouring optional parameters
  and `params`. Overloads of equal arity are not told apart by argument type: the
  declaring type's own fitting methods win, several fitting ones stay as a set only
  if they resolve to one method.
- **Unresolved by design:** calls on `var`, expression results, tuples, extension
  methods, external types (BCL, NuGet), `dynamic`, and names an unknown base type
  could declare.

## Limits and evidence

No oracle against the Roslyn compiler was run: no .NET SDK was available in the
development environment, so resolution is validated by the fixture tests
(`tests/python/test_csharp.py`, `fixtures/csharp_repo`) rather than a compiler. Ranking,
routing and packing are untouched: the ContextBench py gate's `metrics.json` is
byte-identical to `baseline-v21` after the change (only the derivation id differs).

"""Compare OXIDE's resolved C# edges with the Roslyn oracle (scripts/csharp_oracle).

Usage: dotnet scripts/csharp_oracle/... <root> > edges.jsonl
       uv run python scripts/csharp_oracle_compare.py <root> edges.jsonl

A resolved ``calls``/``references`` edge *agrees* when the oracle binds the same site
(file, start) to a declaration inside one of the edge's target entities; it *disagrees*
when the oracle binds that site elsewhere, and is *unbound* when the oracle binds it to
nothing in the tree (external or unresolved there). Recall is the share of oracle edges
OXIDE resolved at the same site.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import derive


def main(root: Path, edges: Path) -> None:
    cap = capture(root)
    texts = {f.path: f.data for f in cap.files if f.path.endswith(".cs")}
    offsets: dict[str, list[int]] = {}

    def byte(path: str, line: int, col: int) -> int:
        if path not in offsets:
            starts, at = [], 0
            for piece in texts[path].splitlines(keepends=True):
                starts.append(at)
                at += len(piece)
            offsets[path] = starts
        text = texts[path][offsets[path][line] :].decode("utf-8", "replace")
        return offsets[path][line] + len(text[:col].encode("utf-8"))

    oracle: dict[tuple[str, str, int], tuple[str, int]] = {}
    for raw in edges.read_text().splitlines():
        e = json.loads(raw)
        f, t = e["from"], e["to"]
        if f["file"] in texts and t["file"] in texts:
            site = (e["kind"], f["file"], byte(f["file"], f["line"], f["col"]))
            oracle[site] = (t["file"], byte(t["file"], t["line"], t["col"]))
    result = derive(cap, "oracle")
    entities = {e.key: e for e in result.entities}
    tally: Counter[str] = Counter()
    seen: set[tuple[str, str, int]] = set()
    bad: list[str] = []
    for e in result.edges:
        if e.kind not in ("calls", "references") or e.resolution != "resolved" or e.evidence is None:
            continue
        kind = "call" if e.kind == "calls" else "ref"
        ev = e.evidence
        if ev.path not in texts or not ev.path.endswith(".cs"):
            continue
        site = (kind, ev.path, ev.start)
        seen.add(site)
        want = oracle.get(site)
        if want is None:
            tally[f"{kind} unbound"] += 1
            continue
        hit = any(
            (s := entities[t].source) is not None
            and s.path == want[0]
            and s.start <= want[1] < s.end
            for t in e.targets
            if t in entities
        )
        tally[f"{kind} {'agree' if hit else 'disagree'}"] += 1
        if not hit and len(bad) < 25:
            bad.append(f"{ev.path}@{ev.start} {e.source} -> {e.targets} oracle {want}")
    for kind in ("call", "ref"):
        found = [s for s in oracle if s[0] == kind]
        tally[f"{kind} oracle-total"] = len(found)
        tally[f"{kind} oracle-resolved-by-oxide"] = sum(s in seen for s in found)
    for k, v in sorted(tally.items()):
        print(f"{k}: {v}")
    print("\n".join(bad))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[2]))

- **Defines:** Newtonsoft.Json needs its `DefineConstants` passed to the oracle. Without them the oracle compiles a different tree and about 760 references looked like disagreements.
- **Bug found and fixed:** the oracle showed my first version dropping inherited overloads when the class had its own method of the same name. The resolver now keeps own and inherited overloads together as candidates, and an `override` hides the base method of the same arity. This made `Store.Put(string,int)` versus the inherited `Put(string,string)` ambiguous, so I changed that fixture test to expect that.
- **Remaining disagreements:** the 4 are overloads the compiler picks by argument type. OXIDE doesn't see argument types, so it picks wrong in those cases.
